what: INTERFACES.md 20: the backtest with rebalancing delays (PLAN.md 6.9 step 9). Money in USD. A minute counts the window's one-minute closes from 0, as RISK_ENGINE.md 13.1 does; null is the window's start, when the loan is drawn. `table` is the README's: for each book and delay, the worst over the windows.
assumptions: Books: RISK_ENGINE.md 13.1's hedged book at full size (1.2774 nBTC, the same BTC short, $35k of margin), and 13.4's directional book ($100k of USDC on NEAR; long $150k SOL, short $100k ETH, long $60k HYPE and $30k kPEPE) with each of the two margins 13.4 gives it, $80k and $200k. All Standard tier, on section 13's market: 4 Nov 2026 prices, a $2M pool with $1.2M lent, so the Standard rate is 6.5%.

The loan: each book draws its full Standard line, worked out by the engine at the window's start, and the money leaves the account (RISK_ENGINE.md 7.2). The pool's $25k first-week limit is left out, as 13.1 does for an account a week old.

Prices: each minute is the engine's own replay path (RISK_ENGINE.md 4.5): recorded one-minute closes, or BTC's path times the window's scale, with the adverse perp gap on every perp and the normal depeg (bridged tokens -2%, USDT -1%) from minute 0 on. The volatility factor stays at the starting market's (1): the replay file holds only the window, not the 720 hours before it. The 1-hour TWAP is the price itself, which only matters for new credit.

Order within a minute: the price moves and a minute of carry accrues; Hyperliquid's replica checks the account first, before money due that minute lands and before we act; then arrivals; then the engine's check; then the keeper's steps; then Hyperliquid checks again at the same marks; money sent with no delay lands at the end of the minute.

Checks: one a minute. A DELEVERAGE plan is confirmed by the check 3 minutes after the first DELEVERAGE verdict, if every check in between also said DELEVERAGE (the contract would take 2 minutes; any other verdict starts the pair again); at once when Hyperliquid's margin ratio is 80% or more. Each confirmation opens the next pair, so a running unwind gets a new plan every 3 minutes. REBALANCE and REBALANCE_NOW plans run at the check that asks.

Plans: the engine's own (deleverage_steps, rebalance_steps), with 1Click's routes, written as at most 4 step objects, whole steps only (a pair is a perp and a sale), as pb-risk writes them. Quotes are always there. Perp sizes are not rounded to Hyperliquid's size decimals, and its $10 minimum is not applied.

Fills: a perp step fills in the minute it runs, at that minute's mark (gap included). Every trade pays the engine's unwind-cost formula (4.6) at the size traded so far in that coin or token during the window, as a marginal cost C(done + this) - C(done), so ten small trades never cost less than one big one.

1Click: a sale is priced at its quote, in the minute it runs, less the engine's 1Click cost; its USDC lands on NEAR after the delay. to_hl and home move USDC after the delay, less 1Click's 0.2 USDC fee. Nothing is refunded, and a transfer is never overdue (its quoted time is the delay).

Money in flight: the engine sees each transfer as the token sent, at 98%, marked with where it goes (pb-read's rule). A REBALANCE takes 98% of the USDC already on its way to Hyperliquid off what it asks for (rebalance_need, since 9 Nov), so while a top-up is in transit a check asks only for what it doesn't cover; the account allows 8 transfers under way. A repay after a sale waits for that sale to land (as built); a newer stored plan replaces the old one, and a plan older than the latest verdict runs no more steps once a verdict says NONE.

The pool's 24-hour limit: sales and transfers past $50k of plan steps in 24 hours need the operator's co-signature (PLAN.md 5.1). By default none comes during the window, so those steps are refused; a pair's perp leg still runs, because the gateway places perp steps on its own (as built). `--cosign` runs with the operator co-signing at once.
Carry: interest accrues each minute on the debt at the tier's normal rate, and funding on each perp at its trailing 30-day rate.

Hyperliquid's replica (RISK_ENGINE.md 4.3) at each minute's marks: below maintenance margin, a book liquidation closes every perp and pays the replica's slippage; below 2/3 of it, the backstop keeps everything. No ADL.

Pool loss: max(0, debt - what the account is worth closed out that minute): NEAR tokens and perps sold at that minute's prices with the costs above, Hyperliquid's side floored at 0 (non-recourse), money in flight at 98% of what it will deliver; never more than the debt.

Equity: the engine's mark equity at each minute's check, before that minute's steps, with that check's IM. The margin-call clock adds each minute that follows a check below MR. The client does nothing during the window.
